items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: when his brother Theodore came down here, with a bunch of guys from Chicago, Murphy Steinberg... They were, they were, they had a band that they patterned off of the, off of the rhythm games.

ctx.x: When you played the dances, they used the snare drum and the bass drum too?

Well, when I first started, yes. Because, uh, another little story about Rag Baby. Uh, incidentally, he has a son who works in the quarter. Yeah. Yeah. Nah. Well, Rag Baby was, uh, he always had, uh, lady troubles. And, uh, he, he was, uh, he, he left his family. I think he had six, seven kids, something like that. And he left to pull out on the family. And the, the police were always hounding him, you know, for alimony. And, uh, my dad would have to carry me along because they, they had places like the Southern…
Well, before I forget, you mentioned that, uh, word double drums. I've heard Papa Lane talk about that. Just what do you mean?
